name: Heavyweight 6-Panel Cap
tagline: 300 gsm cotton twill, six structured panels, and a crown that holds a dense logo.
blurb: The premium blank: dense 300 gsm twill and a stiff front panel that keeps logos crisp.
intro: Most caps are built from 240 to 260 gsm twill. This one runs 300 gsm, a heavier yarn count that gives the crown body and stops the front panel from softening after a season. Six sewn panels, a full buckram front and a pre-curved visor keep the shape square in the box.

It is the blank brands order when the logo is the product: one dense front mark, a small side hit, nothing else. The heavier weave also takes 3D puff better, because the stitches sit on a surface that does not pucker under the tension of a dense stitch block.

features.title: 300 gsm twill
features.text: Roughly 40 gsm heavier than a standard cap, so the crown resists softening and the brim keeps its curve.

features.title: Structured front
features.text: Full buckram backing keeps the panel flat, which holds a 9 cm embroidered mark legible at a distance.

features.title: Holds puff embroidery
features.text: The dense weave carries 3D puff up to 4 mm without the panel puckering underneath the stitch block.

features.title: One size, adjustable
features.text: Metal slide buckle adjusts 56–60 cm; S/M, L/XL and youth bands are cut on the same minimum.

specs: Metal slide buckle with tuck-in strap

faqs.q: What makes this heavier than your other six-panels?
faqs.a: The twill is 300 gsm against 240–260 gsm on a standard cap, and the crown carries a full buckram front rather than a partial one.

faqs.q: Why is it $7.40 at 10 pcs?
faqs.a: The heavier fabric costs more per meter and the structured build takes longer to block, which adds roughly $1.00 over our entry six-panel.

faqs.q: Can I buy it blank for my own decoration?
faqs.a: Yes. Blanks ship in 7–10 days and can be packed flat with no fold crease if your own embroidery shop finishes them.

name: Structured Fitted Cap
tagline: Acrylic-wool fitted crown in half sizes, flat or curved visor, no adjuster.
blurb: True fitted cap with a sewn-in size band and a high structured crown. No strap.
intro: A fitted cap is a size, not a range. The band is sewn in from 6 7/8 to 7 5/8 in half sizes, the crown is blocked on a wooden form, and there is no plastic snap to loosen after a hundred wears. That is why it reads as equipment rather than giveaway.

The acrylic-wool blend holds a pressed shape better than cotton, resists pilling at the band and takes 3D puff cleanly on the front panel. Order a balanced size run across six or seven sizes, or send the size curve from your last program and we will cut to it.

features.title: Half sizes, no adjuster
features.text: 6 7/8 to 7 5/8, each size blocked separately, so the fit does not depend on a strap.

features.title: Pressed on a block
features.text: Steam-pressed over a wooden form after sewing; the crown keeps its shape through packing and wear.

features.title: Flat or curved visor
features.text: Stock build is flat with 6 rows of stitching; we curve it in-house at no charge when specified.

features.title: 3D puff front
features.text: The high front panel carries raised embroidery up to 10 cm wide without visible distortion.

faqs.q: Do I have to order every size?
faqs.a: No, but a fitted run is usually split across five to seven sizes. Send a size curve and we will quote the mix.

faqs.q: Can the visor arrive curved?
faqs.a: Yes. The stock visor is flat; we shape it before packing at no extra cost if it is noted on the order.

faqs.q: Will the wool blend shrink?
faqs.a: Cold hand wash and air dry. Hot water shrinks the band about half a size, and that is not recoverable.

name: Wool Blend Fitted Cap
tagline: Twenty percent wool, on-field crown shape, eight rows of visor stitching.
blurb: Wool-blend fitted cap with the on-field silhouette and dense eight-row visor stitching.
intro: The gap between a wool blend and a straight acrylic cap shows in the hand: the wool adds loft, the crown presses sharper and the fabric does not shine under arena lights. Ours runs 20% wool, enough to change the look without the price of a full wool felt.

Built to the on-field pattern: high structured crown, flat visor, eight rows of stitching across the brim and a fitted band with no adjuster. Half sizes from 6 7/8 to 7 5/8, each blocked individually so a 7 1/4 is actually a 7 1/4 and not a 7 3/8.

features.title: 20% wool blend
features.text: Wool adds loft and a matte surface; the visor keeps its shape instead of curling after a season.

features.title: 8-row visor stitching
features.text: Eight concentric stitch rows at 6 mm spacing, the densest brim build we run.

features.title: On-field pattern
features.text: High crown, flat brim, fitted band and no adjuster — the shape used on the field.

features.title: Blocked per size
features.text: Every half size is pressed on its own form, which keeps sizing consistent between production runs.

faqs.q: How much wool is actually in it?
faqs.a: 20% wool, 80% acrylic. A full wool cap costs about $3 more per piece and runs hotter; the blend keeps the matte look without the heat.

faqs.q: Is the eight-row stitching structural?
faqs.a: It stiffens the visor edge as well as finishing it, which is why the brim stays flat instead of curling over time.

faqs.q: Why does it cost more than the acrylic fitted cap?
faqs.a: The wool content raises the yarn price and the extra stitch rows add machine time, about $1.20 per piece at this quantity.

name: Wordmark Snapback
tagline: Mid-profile snapback with a flat brim, cut for long thin wordmarks.
blurb: Six-panel snapback shaped for wide, thin lettering. Flat brim, plastic snap.
intro: Most snapbacks are built for a badge. This one is built for a line of type: a mid-profile crown, a front panel without heavy buckram support, and a flat brim that keeps the proportions horizontal. Long, thin wordmarks read cleanly across it instead of wrapping around a stiff curve.

The stock build is six panels with a seven-position plastic snap and a cotton twill sweatband. Because the crown sits lower than a high-profile streetwear shape, the cap works as merch for a record label or a coffee brand, not only for a skate drop.

features.title: Made for wide marks
features.text: The flat brim and mid crown give a horizontal field that suits letterforms up to 14 cm wide.

features.title: 7-position snap
features.text: Plastic snapback adjusts about 55–61 cm and does not slip the way a buckle does under daily wear.

features.title: Low front buckram
features.text: Partial support only, so thin lettering sits flat instead of bridging a hard curve.

features.title: Flat brim, 6-row
features.text: Uncurved 7.5 cm visor with six stitch rows; we can pre-curve it on request at no cost.

specs: Flat embroidery, woven patch, screen print

faqs.q: How wide can my wordmark be?
faqs.a: About 14 cm across the front panel before the ends start to drop over the curve. Send the artwork and we scale it in the proof.

faqs.q: Is the brim really flat?
faqs.a: Yes, it ships uncurved. We can curve it before packing if your customers expect a traditional shape.

faqs.q: Can you embroider a strapline under the wordmark?
faqs.a: Yes. A second line of text adds about $0.45 per piece and needs 8 mm of clear space between lines.

name: Foam Front Trucker
tagline: Foam front, mesh back, five panels — the cheapest large-logo build we run.
blurb: Classic foam-front trucker with a mesh back. Biggest flat logo area for the money.
intro: The foam-front trucker is the least expensive way to put a large logo on a cap. The front is a single molded foam panel, so a 12 cm print or patch sits perfectly flat with no curve to fight, and the mesh back keeps both the cost and the weight down.

It is a five-panel build with a snapback, which suits promo, farm supply, landscaping, fishing and event work across the U.S. South and Midwest, where a cheap cap that breathes matters more than a fashion shape. Bright foam colors are stock; we dye to a Pantone reference from 100 pcs per colorway.

features.title: 12 cm flat field
features.text: The molded foam front takes a 12 cm wide print or patch with no curvature distortion.

features.title: Breathes in heat
features.text: Poly mesh back panels move air; it is the coolest cap in the range in direct sun.

features.title: Lowest decoration cost
features.text: Screen print on foam is our cheapest method, about $0.30 per piece at volume.

features.title: Five-panel front
features.text: No center seam across the front, so a single wide mark stays uninterrupted.

specs: Poly foam front, poly mesh back
Screen print, flat embroidery, woven patch

faqs.q: Why is the carton larger than a twill cap?
faqs.a: Foam fronts do not compress. A 100-pc carton runs about 0.18 cbm against 0.15 for twill, so freight per piece is slightly higher.

faqs.q: Can the mesh be a color other than white?
faqs.a: Yes, contrast mesh is available from 100 pcs per colorway; stock builds ship with white mesh.

faqs.q: Is embroidery possible on the foam front?
faqs.a: Yes, but keep it under 8 cm wide. Larger embroidery pulls the foam and leaves a visible ring.

name: Contrast Mesh Trucker
tagline: Two-tone trucker with contrast mesh, a piped brim and a snapback closure.
blurb: Two-tone trucker with contrast mesh and piping. A promo cap that looks designed.
intro: The foam-front trucker is cheap; the two-tone version looks expensive. Contrast mesh against the front panel, piping along the visor edge and a snapback closure turn a giveaway into something a retailer will hang on a peg instead of dropping it into a clearance bin.

Piping is the detail that separates this from a plain trucker: a corded edge in a third color runs the whole visor line and picks up the mesh tone. Stock builds ship in four two-tone combinations; custom Pantone splits start at 100 pcs per colorway, with a matched under-brim.

features.title: Contrast mesh
features.text: A second color in the back mesh and under-brim adds depth without extra decoration cost.

features.title: Corded visor piping
features.text: Piping runs the visor edge in a third color, the detail that reads as a designed cap.

features.title: Molded foam front
features.text: Still holds a 12 cm flat logo area; the two-tone build limits nothing about decoration.

features.title: Snapback closure
features.text: Seven-position plastic snap, about 55–61 cm, better for shared stock than a buckle.

specs: Poly foam front, contrast poly mesh back
Screen print, flat embroidery, woven patch

faqs.q: Is the piping a separate material?
faqs.a: It is a braided cord sewn into the visor seam, matched to the mesh color or set to a third color at your choice.

faqs.q: Can the mesh and piping be different colors?
faqs.a: Yes. Crown, mesh and piping can each be a different color inside the same per-colorway minimum.

faqs.q: Does the two-tone build cost more?
faqs.a: About $0.55 per piece over the single-tone trucker, which covers the extra cutting and color matching, not the materials.

name: Tour Golf Cap
tagline: Laser-perforated technical tour cap with a moisture-wicking sweatband.
blurb: Tour-shaped performance cap: perforated panels, wicking band, structured front.
intro: A tour cap has to look technical without looking like a running hat. This one is built on a low structured crown with laser-perforated side panels, a wicking sweatband and a matte poly shell that does not shine under a camera flash or a clubhouse light.

The perforations are laser cut, not punched, so the hole edges stay clean through repeated washing. Fabric weight is around 165 gsm, light enough for a July round on a humid afternoon and dense enough to hold a structured front panel and a crisp embroidered mark.

features.title: Laser-cut vents
features.text: Perforations are cut by laser rather than punched, so edges do not fray and the pattern stays even.

features.title: Wicking sweatband
features.text: Poly band with an antimicrobial finish pulls sweat off the brow and dries in minutes.

features.title: Structured low crown
features.text: Light buckram keeps the front flat without the height of a streetwear crown.

features.title: Matte finish
features.text: A dull poly surface that photographs without glare, which is why tour caps look expensive on camera.

faqs.q: Do the perforations weaken the crown?
faqs.a: No. They are limited to the side panels, which carry no structural load, and the front keeps a full buckram backing.

faqs.q: Is this the same body as your performance golf cap?
faqs.a: Same pattern family, but this build uses a lighter 165 gsm matte shell and a lower crown height.

faqs.q: Can I print instead of embroider?
faqs.a: Yes, sublimation and heat transfer both work on the poly shell; embroidery holds up longer on the structured front.

name: Piqué Golf Cap
tagline: Cotton piqué golf cap with a metal buckle and a classic club profile.
blurb: Piqué cotton, mid crown, brass buckle. The clubhouse cap without the club markup.
intro: Piqué is the polo-shirt weave: a small raised diamond that gives cotton texture and lets air through. On a cap it reads as clubhouse rather than sportswear, which is why pro shops and resort accounts order it over a technical shell. It also creases less than plain twill after a day in a golf bag.

The build is deliberately traditional: six panels, mid-profile structured crown, curved visor and an antique brass slide buckle with a fabric tuck strap. Embroidered club marks sit well on the piqué surface, and the weave hides the slight puckering that flat twill shows along the seam under dense stitching.

features.title: Piqué weave
features.text: A raised diamond texture that breathes better than plain twill and hides creasing in a bag.

features.title: Brass buckle
features.text: Antique brass slide buckle and fabric tuck strap instead of a plastic snap.

features.title: Club proportions
features.text: Mid-profile crown and a 7 cm curved visor, the shape a pro shop expects to see.

features.title: Tonal or contrast mark
features.text: Cream on navy or white on forest; the weave holds fine 2 mm lettering cleanly.

specs: Flat embroidery, woven patch, screen print

faqs.q: Will piqué shrink when washed?
faqs.a: Expect up to 2% on the first cold wash. We cut with that allowance, so the fit after washing matches the stated size.

faqs.q: Can I get this in a technical poly piqué?
faqs.a: Yes, a poly piqué version exists at the same price and dries faster; ask for it when you request the quote.

faqs.q: Is the buckle solid brass?
faqs.a: Antique brass finish over zinc alloy. Solid brass is available from 300 pcs at about $0.40 more per piece.

name: Performance Golf Visor
tagline: Open-top visor with a wide wicking band and a laser-perforated brim.
blurb: Open-top performance visor. Wide wicking band, low glare, built for summer rounds.
intro: A visor solves the problem a cap creates: heat. With the crown open, air moves over the head, and a wide band still catches sweat before it reaches the eyes. Ours uses a 4.5 cm band with a wicking lining rather than the thin elastic band on a promotional visor.

The brim is a poly twill with a matte finish and laser-perforated vents on the top surface, so it does not turn into a heat trap in direct sun. One size with an elastic back section fits roughly 55–59 cm and has no visible adjuster to break.

features.title: Wide 4.5 cm band
features.text: A broad band with a wicking lining catches sweat before it reaches the brow.

features.title: Open crown
features.text: No crown means maximum airflow; the coolest option in the range for July events.

features.title: Perforated brim
features.text: Laser vents in the brim surface stop heat building on top of the head.

features.title: Hidden elastic
features.text: An elastic back section holds 55–59 cm with no plastic tab or buckle showing.

specs: Open top, 4.5 cm band, structured brim

faqs.q: Does an open visor stay on during a swing?
faqs.a: Yes, if the band is sized correctly. The elastic holds 55–59 cm; larger heads should take the XL band, which we cut at 60 cm.

faqs.q: Can I put a logo on the band?
faqs.a: Up to 6 cm wide on the front of the band, embroidered or heat transferred. Wider marks wrap around the curve.

faqs.q: Is this unisex?
faqs.a: Yes. The band is one size and the brim is 7 cm deep, which suits most women and men without a separate pattern.

name: Knit Band Visor
tagline: Soft knit band visor that packs flat, with an elastic back and no hardware.
blurb: Knit-band visor that folds into a bag. Elastic back, no hardware, travel-ready.
intro: This visor is built around a soft knit band rather than a stiff shell, so it can be folded in half and pushed into a golf bag without taking a permanent crease. It comes out looking the way it went in, which is useful for resort shops that hand them out at the first tee.

The band is a two-layer knit with a cotton-facing inner edge, and the brim is a light cotton-nylon blend with a sewn edge rather than a molded plastic core. One size fits 54–59 cm on the hidden elastic, and the whole visor weighs just under 60 g.

features.title: Packs flat
features.text: No rigid band or plastic brim core, so it folds and recovers without a permanent crease.

features.title: Soft knit band
features.text: Two-layer knit with a cotton-facing inner edge that does not scratch the forehead.

features.title: Under 60 g
features.text: Light enough to forget you are wearing it, and cheap to ship in a padded mailer.

features.title: Elastic back
features.text: Hidden elastic covers 54–59 cm with no visible tab or buckle.

specs: Woven label, heat transfer, flat embroidery

faqs.q: Does it lose shape after packing?
faqs.a: No. The band has no rigid core, so it recovers as soon as it is worn; that is the whole reason it exists as a travel SKU.

faqs.q: How does sizing work without an adjuster?
faqs.a: Elastic covers 54–59 cm. Outside that range the band will pinch or sit loose, so we do not recommend it for XL programs.

faqs.q: Can I embroider the band?
faqs.a: A woven label or heat transfer is the better choice; embroidery on a knit band adds bulk and can pucker the band.

name: Featherweight Running Cap
tagline: 90 gsm micro poly running cap with an optional reflective trim.
blurb: Featherweight running cap in 90 gsm micro poly. Low profile, reflective option.
intro: At 90 gsm the shell is about half the weight of a standard cotton cap, and the finished piece comes in near 55 g. That matters on a long run: less fabric to soak, faster drying, and no heavy buckram pressing on the forehead after twenty minutes.

The pattern is low profile with a short 6 cm visor, so it sits under a helmet or a hood without lifting. Reflective trim can be added along the visor edge and the back seam, which makes it a practical option for early and late training.

features.title: 90 gsm shell
features.text: About half the weight of cotton twill; the finished cap is close to 55 g.

features.title: Reflective option
features.text: Retroreflective tape along the visor edge and back seam, available from 100 pcs.

features.title: Low profile
features.text: Short 6 cm visor and a shallow crown that sit under a helmet or a hood.

features.title: Dries fast
features.text: Micro poly knit releases water quickly, so a soaked cap is dry in about 20 minutes in sun.

faqs.q: Does the reflective trim cost extra?
faqs.a: About $0.60 per piece from 100 pcs, applied to the visor edge and the back seam.

faqs.q: Will it fit under a bike helmet?
faqs.a: Yes. The 6 cm visor and shallow crown were cut for that; it also fits under a hood without pushing the brim down.

faqs.q: Is 90 gsm too thin to hold a logo?
faqs.a: Heat transfer and small embroidery both work. Keep embroidery under 6 cm wide and backed, or the thin knit will pucker.

name: Tennis Club Cap
tagline: Five-panel tennis cap with a short visor and a light cotton blend shell.
blurb: Short-visor five-panel in light cotton blend. Made for courts, clubs and resort shops.
intro: Tennis caps are cut short on purpose: a 6 cm visor keeps the ball in view on an overhead, and a five-panel crown sits close enough to stay put through a serve. This one is built on a light cotton blend at about 180 gsm, cool enough for a full match.

The palette is club rather than sport: cream, navy, forest and clay, with contrast visor options that pick up the court color. A metal buckle keeps the back clean and flat, and the short visor means the cap reads as tennis from thirty feet away.

features.title: Short 6 cm visor
features.text: Cut short so an overhead does not disappear behind the brim.

features.title: Five-panel crown
features.text: No center seam, sits close, and stays put through a serve.

features.title: Light cotton blend
features.text: About 180 gsm, cool enough for a full match and structured enough to hold a mark.

features.title: Metal buckle
features.text: Antique brass buckle and tuck strap, a cleaner back than a plastic snap.

specs: Flat embroidery, woven patch, screen print

faqs.q: Why is the visor shorter than a standard cap?
faqs.a: It is a tennis-specific cut: a 6 cm brim keeps the ball visible when you look up for a lob or a serve.

faqs.q: Is this cap unisex?
faqs.a: Yes, one size at 55–59 cm with a buckle. A youth band at 52–55 cm is available on the same minimum.

faqs.q: Can I order a matching visor?
faqs.a: Yes, the knit band visor can be built in the same fabric and colorway for a two-SKU club order.
